summary.text: Alan Menadue is an independent candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His website says he grew up in country Victoria, served as a sergeant in the RAAF from 1981 to 1992, has never owned a home and lives in community housing in Prahran. He has stood as an independent in Prahran at the 2014, 2018 and 2022 state elections and at the 2025 by-election.

priorities.text: Standing up for renters and helping them into homes of their own
Government at every level that represents people from the bottom up
Equality as the test for laws, the idea behind his '1 (=) 1' philosophy

summary.text: Angelica Di Camillo is the Greens candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election. She is an environmental engineer who also works in project management and climate strategy, teaches Pilates and lives in St Kilda East. She has run for the Greens three times before: in Rowville at the 2022 state election, at the 2023 federal by-election in Aston, and in Prahran at the February 2025 by-election, losing each time.

occupation.text: Environmental engineer, project manager and climate strategist

priorities.text: Relief for renters and action on the housing crisis
Reducing inequality, funded by higher taxes on big corporations
Speaking up for young people, families and small businesses
I will never take corporate donations

summary.text: Clayton Doueihi is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election. He works in hospitality and retail and belongs to the United Workers Union. For several years he has been a community activist, organising rallies in support of Palestinians and against the far right.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's results list a Victorian Socialists candidate named Clayton Doueihi; same name and party, but no source we read says it was him.

priorities.text: Challenging energy companies, supermarkets, banks and insurers over living costs
Electing working-class representatives who organise in workplaces and on the streets
If elected, I'll fight for you.

summary.text: Daniel O'Neill, on the VEC's list of nominations as G. Daniel O'Neill, is the Animal Justice Party's candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election. The party's page and the ABC named him for Albert Park before nominations closed, and Wikipedia listed him first on its Southern Metropolitan Region ticket. An equity, diversity and inclusion consultant, he grew up in Sydney, has worked for more than 25 years across universities, government, business and charities, and became an authorised marriage celebrant in 2018.

prior_roles.note: The party page says he became a celebrant in 2018; it does not say whether he still practises.

priorities.text: Animal welfare to be weighed in every law, policy and public decision
Stronger protection for native wildlife, including the dingo
Humane, evidence-based control of introduced species
Rewilding urban habitat and waterways for pollinators and other wildlife

summary.text: Meghan Hopper is the Labor candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election. She lectures in media, film and journalism at Monash University, earlier managed community and corporate planning at Moonee Valley City Council, and won a seat on Stonnington City Council in 2024. She also stood for Labor in Warrandyte at the 2010 state election.

occupation.text: Lecturer, School of Media, Film and Journalism, Monash University

prior_roles.note: The ABC and Labor say she has served as a mayor without naming the council. Wikipedia lists a Labor councillor named Meghan Hopper as mayor of Moreland in 2014-15 and does not list her among Stonnington's mayors; no source we read confirms which council.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's results list a Labor candidate named Meghan Hopper; same name and party, but no source we read says it was her.

priorities.text: Affordable housing and easing cost-of-living pressures
Access to a strong public education for every local young person

summary.text: Morgan Jonas is the Safety Victoria – Violent Crime Prevention candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations, and is the party's registered officer. Jonas founded and leads the party, which was registered in 2022 as the Freedom Party of Victoria on a platform opposing COVID-19 lockdowns and vaccine mandates and took its current name in 2026. Jonas headed the Freedom Party's South-Eastern Metropolitan ticket at the 2022 state election and ran for the Senate in Victoria as a grouped independent that year.

prior_roles.organisation: Freedom Party of Victoria (Safety Victoria – Violent Crime Prevention from 2026)

previous_candidacies.note: Freedom Party of Victoria; first on the ticket.
Grouped independent, first on the group's ticket, endorsed by Reignite Democracy Australia.

summary.text: Rachel Westaway is the Liberal MP for Prahran, which she took from the Greens at a by-election in February 2025 after Sam Hibbins resigned. Before entering Parliament she sat on the Administrative Appeals Tribunal as a senior member for over 20 years, after an earlier marketing career. Since January 2026 she has been a shadow assistant minister, including for Melbourne. She is recontesting Prahran in 2026.

summary.text: Tosh-Jake Finnigan is an independent candidate for Prahran at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Finnigan founded the Restore Democracy Sack Dan Andrews Party in 2022 over Labor's 'red shirts' affair and headed its Western Victoria upper-house ticket that year (listed as Jake Finnigan); the party was deregistered in December 2023. Finnigan joined Colac Otway Shire Council on a countback in January 2023 and was not re-elected at the 2024 council election.
summary.note: No source names the Prahran candidate as the founder of the Restore Democracy Sack Dan Andrews Party and former Colac Otway councillor; the match rests on the uncommon name.

prior_roles.organisation: Restore Democracy Sack Dan Andrews Party

previous_candidacies.note: Not elected in 2020; joined the council on a countback in 2023.
Restore Democracy Sack Dan Andrews Party; first on the ticket, listed as Jake Finnigan.
